questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I prioritized a destination that offered opportunities to immerse myself in a new culture, as broadening my cultural horizons and understanding diverse perspectives are integral to my personal and academic growth. Additionally, I considered the academic reputation of the host institution and its alignment with my field of study, ensuring that it could complement and enhance my academic journey. Lastly, practical factors such as the destination's accessibility, safety, and the availability of resources to support international students were important in making an informed choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thoroughly enjoyed my study abroad experience, however, I believe the educational component could have been stronger. While the courses were interesting, I felt that the general level was much lower when compared to University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Monash University made it incredibly easy to settle in upon arrival. The university provided a comprehensive orientation program, which included campus tours, sessions to familiarize students with local culture and university resources, and opportunities to meet other exchange students. Additionally, the support staff were readily available to answer any questions, and the pre-arrival materials ensured a smooth transition.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very good!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding off-campus accommodation in Melbourne was not very easy since everything was super expensive or you would need to rent the place for at least 6 months. I recommend not spending time on the traditional real-estate agencies but instead use Facebook groups such as "Fairy Floss" or apps like "Flatmates". You might also get lucky through Airbnb

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is more expensive than living on campus, although the experience is worth the higher price. I would definitely recommend finding roommates to split the expenses. Also, I can be difficult to find a place and therefore you need to spend some time doing it. I don't recommend finding a place before going and seeing it, since I had a lot of friends who got something that was far from what they were promised. Instead, we rented an Airbnb for the first two weeks to we had the time to find a place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very limited supply of student accommodation

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super easy. If you had any questions the on-campus staff was super friendly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will need to enrol in their digital systems. Once you are accepted to the University you receive an email with clear guidelines on how to activate your account. They operate with multiple digital systems but navigating them was super easy and user-friendly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have on-campus it help (Clayton campus) and a call center. Went down there multiple times myself and they were very kind.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was enrolled to all the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find some courses that you think sound interesting and also a few others. Once you get there you have two weeks to change courses. If one of the pre-selected courses did not live up to your expectations then you can easily take another one instead.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, the lecturers were super good but the general level among students was not very good when compared to University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As described above, the level of the MA-program was much easier than at my home institution. The teachers was actually super good but the other students did not participate enough to increase the overall level of classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was the same. We had both lecturers and tutorials. One thing that is different is that they focus a lot more on active participation. Therefor, you will need to be prepared in order to answer the questions from the lecturer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Mergers & Acquisitions 
Corporate Financing Decisions 
Startup Finance & Accounting 
Startup Fundamentals: From setting up to securing investment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the courses I had was great if you like the world of finance

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than anticipated. Also, housing can be very expensive if you don't live together with somebody.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A huge variety of University clubs to take part in. Everything from surfing to chess. Also they have a gym at Caufield, which is less expensive than regular gyms.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could do everything you wanted in terms of sports. They also have debate clubs, cooking courses etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find a sport that you like or want to be good at. Often they meet twice a week and by this you make some very good friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the many different national parks around Melbourne such as Wilsons Prometary, Phillip Island and The Great Ocean Road.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy. People are very friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the events and social activities they do at university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They were super friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be actively involved in the events at University. You will meet great friend there. 
Be curious about courses. Maybe try something that is not as close to what you usually do- you will learn a lot
Enjoy your time. Time flies and before you know it you are back againg. Make sure to do some nice things during the weekends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have mentioned all important elements

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live in a different city. You met so many other exchange students and had so much fun hanging out with them. Going to university in a different place also required you to be super proactive in terms of finding new friends and working together on school assignments.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Although there are many Danish students going to Melbourne, try to find some local friends also. They know a lot more about the city and you will get fun experiences.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
